review_candidates.title: Senior Satellite Systems Engineer
review_candidates.description: Your mission Join us in safeguarding the sustainability of space operations through advanced space situational awareness (SSA) technologies. As part of our team, you will develop cutting-edge collision avoidance algorithms, enhance space situational awareness, and innovate tools for satellite operators. Your expertise in data science and physics will help us detect, predict, and mitigate orbital risks, ensuring safe and sustainable space exploration. Your Tasks And Responsibilities Reviewing and coordinating reviews of Product Assurance & Safety Plan (PASP) and Product Assurance Requirements Documents (PARD) ⁠Performing of end-to-end mission designs tailored to customer needs Assessing customer mission requirements and designing tailored solutions ⁠Identifying customer needs and ideating new solutions Shape our end-to-end mission design software development Reviewing of hardware designs at system and subsystem level Support launch preparation, environmental test campaigns planning, and readiness reviews ahead of launch Compute system budgets (link, power, data) and track margins against requirements throughout development Your profile Must-haves M.Sc. or higher in Aerospace/Space Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, or another relevant technical field. 5+ years of experience in satellite systems engineering with responsibility for system-level engineering activities across major spacecraft development phases, including development, integration, verification, qualification, and launch preparation. 2+ years of experience working within ECSS-compliant development programmes, including technical documentation, formal reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR, QR, AR), and certification activities. Experience contributing to at least one satellite mission that successfully entered operational service. Growth mindset and expanding your horizon Willingness to travel and to work in concentrated review campaigns. English proficiency C1 or better. Valid EU work authorization. Nice-to-haves Familiarity with ECSS product assurance practices (FMEA/FMECA, fault tree analysis, critical items lists, RAMS, ECSS-Q-ST-80C) Experience in Earth observation missions Experience with synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging Why us? With a lean hierarchy and small working groups, you define your own way of work including flexible work hours. Work on groundbreaking space sustainability challenges with a team of top-tier engineers and scientists. After your on-boarding time in Braunschweig, you can choose between staying in our office (what we prefer), working remote (within Germany) or a hybrid approach. Enjoy technical freedom. Influence system architecture, research methodologies, and data integration approaches. Grow continuously with access to training budgets, industry conferences, and networking opportunities. Be part of a strong engineering culture, with regular knowledge-sharing sessions, technical deep dives, and innovation sprints. Great team spirit, with company-wide events such as monthly all-hands lunches, and social activities like laser tag, dinners, and team-building outings. From Application to Offer: Our Hiring Process You send us your application We review your profile and get back to you with a short questionnaire A first interview with our HR team A second interview with a member of the team you would join A final interview with the department lead About Us OKAPI:Orbits is at the forefront of space sustainability, addressing some of the most pressing challenges of the space industry: the growing problem of crowded orbital regimes, and the need for more efficient satellite operations. We're providing end-to-end solutions that help various space industry players cover their Space Situation Awareness (SSA), and Space Traffic Management and Coordination (STM & STC) needs. We are committed to safeguarding space missions and access to space for all humanity. Join us on our mission. Last but not least, we would like to share with you that research shows that women are less likely to apply for a position unless they meet 100% of the listed requirements. Please know that if it’s your case — but you are passionate about space technology, building reliable software, and contributing to a more sustainable space environment — we strongly encourage you to apply. OKAPI:Orbits already brings together a highly diverse team, and we actively continue to strengthen this diversity which allows us to achieve higher performance and drive innovation.

review_candidates.title: Associate Technical Lead – Azure DevOps
review_candidates.description: We’re looking for a hands-on Associate Technical Lead to design, build, and operate our Microsoft Azure infrastructure. You’ll lead technical decisions around Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), infrastructure automation, and GitOps-based delivery. You’ll also work with development teams to improve how they deploy and operate applications, while mentoring engineers on DevOps practices and cloud architecture. Key Responsibilities Design, provision, and maintain secure, scalable, and reliable Azure infrastructure using Terraform or Bicep. Architect and operate Docker-based workloads on AKS. Manage cluster provisioning, upgrades, node pools, autoscaling, workload scheduling, and cost optimisation. Configure Kubernetes ingress, network policies, namespaces, role-based access control (RBAC), resource quotas, and managed identities. Integrate Azure Key Vault with Kubernetes for secrets management. Design and manage Azure networking, including virtual networks, subnets, peering, and private endpoints. Lead GitOps adoption using Argo CD to manage infrastructure and application configuration through version control. Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps Pipelines or GitHub Actions to automate builds, tests, and deployments. Set up observability across metrics, logs, and traces, and maintain dashboards and alerts. Partner with development teams to embed vulnerability scanning, policy enforcement, and compliance checks into delivery workflows. Guide engineers on technical decisions, review infrastructure changes, and document operational practices through runbooks and guides. Requirements 5+ years of overall experience , including at least 2 years in DevOps or cloud engineering . Hands-on experience with Docker, including writing Dockerfiles, creating multi-stage builds, and troubleshooting container networking and volumes. Experience operating AKS clusters, including cluster lifecycle management, workload deployment, autoscaling, and node pool management. Familiarity with taints, tolerations, and workload scheduling. Working knowledge of Kubernetes resources, including Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs, and namespaces. Experience with Azure App Service, Azure Container Registry, Azure Virtual Network, and Azure Load Balancer, along with familiarity with Azure identity and access management, managed identities, and RBAC. Experience configuring Kubernetes ingress controllers, TLS termination, and routing rules. Experience with cert-manager and secrets management using Azure Key Vault or equivalent tools. Experience implementing GitOps with Argo CD or a similar tool and building CI/CD pipelines with Azure DevOps Pipelines or GitHub Actions. Hands-on experience with Terraform or Bicep for Azure infrastructure. This includes writing reusable Terraform modules and managing state and plan/apply workflows, or authoring Bicep templates and modules and deploying them through the Azure CLI or CI/CD pipelines. Experience building dashboards and configuring monitoring and alerts with Prometheus, Grafana, Azure Monitor, or equivalent tools. Ability to take ownership of production issues, explain technical trade-offs clearly, and guide engineers through design and operational decisions. Nice to Have Experience with Helm, service mesh technologies such as Istio or Linkerd, or multi-region AKS deployments. Familiarity with DevSecOps tooling such as Trivy, Checkov, and static or dynamic application security testing. Bash or Python scripting for automation and operational tooling. Experience with the LGTM observability stack (Loki, Grafana, Tempo, and Mimir). Production experience with Kafka or Kafka-compatible systems, including high-throughput event streaming. Experience working directly with clients or across engineering and business teams. Relevant certifications such as AZ-104, AZ-400, CKA, or CKAD.
